requirement.statement: This retained edition of 23EC52 applies in the specified intermediary capacity for the whole interval.
This retained edition of 26EC22 applies to the entity, product, activity and whole assessment interval, with relevant conditions, amendments and relaxations accounted for.
The assessment concerns controls before commencement of that identified related activity.
The Tokenised Securities at issue are securities which this intermediary intends to deal in or advise on.
Assume a separately justified sufficient rule for this scope: A ledger entry establishes customer access
Assume a separately justified sufficient rule for this scope: A reconciliation event establishes proper records
Assume a separately justified sufficient rule for this scope: A recorded relationship establishes the assessed duty
Assume a separately justified sufficient rule for this scope: A remediation event cures the earlier incident
Assume a separately justified sufficient rule for this scope: A supervision event supplies adequate supervision
Assume a separately justified sufficient rule for this scope: Changed terms have been accepted

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Reading B treats the unqualified footnote demonstration wording as standing; the contrary main-text condition is retained.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Reading C attaches footnote minimum content to the main-text request-triggered demonstration.
The assessed entity acts as intermediary for the specified activity, product and period.
The intermediary issues or is substantially involved in issuance of the assessed Tokenised Securities.
The assessed entity is the management company for this scheme and period.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1 support a continuing responsibility requirement; this rule does not select a discharge test.
Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Represent the paragraph 11 requirement separately from paragraph 10 sufficiency.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Reading A takes the express main-text request condition for demonstration; footnote 5's object and standard remain disputed.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: The inserted request condition attaches to demonstration; confirmation is represented separately.
An applicable SFC request for paragraph 14 demonstration covers the assessed activity and interval.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Preserve this paragraph's own SFC request, activity and object; a different request does not satisfy it.
An applicable SFC request for paragraph 15 third-party audit or verification covers the assessed activity and interval.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Preserve this paragraph's own SFC request, activity and object; a different request does not satisfy it.
An applicable SFC request for paragraph 16 satisfactory legal opinion covers the application and interval.
The assessed entity has the Product Provider role for this product and activity throughout the assessment interval.

A customer-access event is recorded for the exact assessed identities, with declared validity covering the assessment interval and known by its cutoff; this does not establish legal sufficiency or the underlying event's truth.

A ledger-entry event is recorded for the exact assessed identities, with declared validity covering the assessment interval and known by its cutoff; this does not establish legal sufficiency or the underlying event's truth.

A terms-acceptance event is recorded for the exact assessed identities, with declared validity covering the assessment interval and known by its cutoff; this does not establish legal sufficiency or the underlying event's truth.

A terms-change event is recorded for the exact assessed identities, with declared validity covering the assessment interval and known by its cutoff; this does not establish legal sufficiency or the underlying event's truth.

A trust-relationship event is recorded for the exact assessed identities, with declared validity covering the assessment interval and known by its cutoff; this does not establish legal sufficiency or the underlying event's truth.
The entity is the scheme or, for a unit trust, the trustee or person appointed by that trustee to maintain the register.
The Commission has made an applicable request for the address where this register is kept.
The intermediary deals in, advises on or manages portfolios investing in the assessed Tokenised Securities.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Retain both issuance involvement and intention to deal in or advise on the specified securities.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Read paragraph 18 within paragraph 17's dealing, advising and portfolio activities.
This retained UT provision applies to this scheme and actor for the whole assessment interval, including actual conditions and relaxations.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Conditionally render the first sentence's shall as MUST, preserving its valuation-specific actor and activity.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: The second sentence uses should for supervision and review; keep it separate from the first sentence's shall.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Keep the requested register-address disclosure distinct from continuous register maintenance.

Assume this source-to-rule interpretation, including its stated trigger, object, standard and applicability transfer: Preserve the scheme/trustee/appointed-person role disjunction; do not assign every Product Provider this role.
A third party is engaged in valuation of this scheme's assets within the scope of UT 6.11C.

heads.question: Does this scope carry the proposed paragraph 10 retained-responsibility requirement?
heads.consequence: Retain ultimate responsibility for management, operational soundness and ownership record keeping regardless of outsourcing.

heads.question: Does the proposed separate paragraph 11 records and compatibility duty apply?
heads.consequence: Ensure proper ownership-interest records are maintained and the arrangement is operationally compatible with involved service providers.

heads.question: Is confirmation required on the proposed paragraph 14 reading?
heads.consequence: Confirm management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity to the SFC.

heads.question: Under reading A, is paragraph 14 demonstration triggered?
heads.consequence: Demonstrate to the SFC's satisfaction the paragraph 14 subjects: management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity.

heads.question: Under reading B, is the standing footnote 5 demonstration duty triggered?
heads.consequence: Demonstrate at least compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

heads.question: Under reading C, is request-triggered demonstration of footnote 5 minimum content required?
heads.consequence: Demonstrate to the SFC's satisfaction at least compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

heads.question: Does the separately requested p15-audit duty apply?
heads.consequence: Obtain third-party audit or verification on management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity.

heads.question: Does the separately requested p16-opinion duty apply?
heads.consequence: Obtain satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application.

heads.question: Does the proposed UT 6.8 register-maintenance duty apply?
heads.consequence: Maintain the register of holders in the specified register-keeper capacity.

heads.question: Does the proposed UT 6.8 requested-address duty apply?
heads.consequence: Advise the Commission of the address where the register is kept.

heads.question: Does the proposed mandatory third-party valuation selection and monitoring duty apply?
heads.consequence: Exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in selecting, appointing and monitoring the valuation third party, including the stated knowledge, experience and resources criterion.

heads.question: Does the proposed valuation-outsourcing supervision and review duty apply?
heads.consequence: Subject the third party's valuation activities to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.

heads.question: Does the proposed issuance responsibility rule apply in this intermediary capacity?
heads.consequence: Remain responsible for the overall tokenisation operation notwithstanding outsourcing.

heads.question: Does the proposed pre-activity controls assessment duty apply?
heads.consequence: Understand and be satisfied with issuer and vendor controls for ownership and technology risks before the related activity.
